nodes.label: Binary Black Hole Merger Feasibility Assessment
nodes.norm_label: binary black hole merger feasibility assessment

nodes.label: Path (a): Full Numerical Relativity
nodes.rationale: Requires solving Einstein's field equations on a dynamical merging spacetime with adaptive mesh refinement and constraint-preserving evolution on HPC clusters; categorically out of scope for a browser-based JavaScript project, no honest smaller version exists.

nodes.label: Path (b): Post-Newtonian Inspiral Approximation
nodes.rationale: A tractable middle ground giving an approximate two-body metric and orbital-decay trajectory via the gravitational-wave energy-loss/quadrupole formula, implementable in JS at effort comparable to or larger than the existing Kerr-Newman module; breaks down near merger, so it can only honestly render early-to-mid inspiral, not merger/ringdown.

nodes.label: Simulator Design Principle: Demonstrate Real Computed Physics
nodes.norm_label: simulator design principle: demonstrate real computed physics
nodes.rationale: The RK4 convergence tests, the analytical-comparison validation suite in runScientificValidation(), and conserved-quantity drift checks exist specifically to demonstrate the simulator computes real physics rather than approximating an effect visually; even approximations (disk, lensing table) are approximations of quantities the solver actually computes, not fabricated trajectories.

nodes.label: Stationary Kerr-Newman Metric Assumption
nodes.rationale: The entire physics layer (metric, metricDerivatives, christoffelSymbols, geodesicRightHandSide, integrateGeodesic) is built around one fixed {M,a,q} stationary solution; a binary system is non-stationary, generally non-axisymmetric and not closed-form during merger, so none of the existing machinery carries over without a wholesale redesign.

nodes.label: Path (c): Purely Visual Non-Physical Merger Approximation
nodes.norm_label: path (c): purely visual non-physical merger approximation
nodes.rationale: Cheap to build (blend/morph two black-hole visuals along a hand-authored trajectory with no solved geodesics) but would be the first feature in the codebase that is purely illustrative with no underlying solved equations, breaking the simulator's core principle of computing real physics rather than approximating visually.
